lines.text: What would happen if the Sun completely turned off for twenty-four hours?
Because sunlight takes eight minutes to reach us, nobody on Earth would notice a thing for the first eight minutes.
Then, pitch black darkness would engulf the daytime hemisphere in a terrifying instant.
Global temperatures would drop noticeably by ten to fifteen degrees, frosting windshields everywhere.
Photosynthesis would pause and birds would frantically roost thinking night arrived early.
Yet because Earth's thick atmosphere retains geothermal heat, humanity would survive the short blackout.
When the blazing light burst back twenty-four hours later, it would be the most celebrated sunrise in history.
